record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: In the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, is every embedded free boundary minimal annulus congruent, up to rigid motions of B^3, to the critical catenoid? Equivalently, is the critical catenoid the unique embedded free boundary minimal annulus in B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 5. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions in B^3) embedded free boundary minimal annulus in B^3?
We call K^{n−1} the (n − 1)-dimensional critical catenoid. When n = 3, we simply call it the critical catenoid denoted by K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ denote the open unit ball with boundary $S^2 = \partial B^3$. A properly immersed surface $\Sigma \subset \overline{B^3}$ with $\partial \Sigma \subset S^2$ is called a free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ if it has zero mean curvature in its interior and meets $S^2$ orthogonally along $\partial \Sigma$. The critical catenoid is the unique (up to rigid motions of $B^3$) piece of a suitably rescaled catenoid $\{(x,y,z) : \sqrt{x^2+y^2} = c\cosh(z/c)\}$ that defines a free boundary minimal annulus in $B^3$.

Prove or disprove: Every embedded free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ that is topologically an annulus is congruent, via a rigid motion of $B^3$, to the critical catenoid.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the well-known critical catenoid conjecture (sometimes attributed to Fraser–Li). Until recently it had been verified only under extra symmetry hypotheses (e.g., reflection symmetry, antipodal symmetry, or two congruent boundary components). A January 2025 preprint by L. Sun ("Free boundary minimal surfaces and the reflection principle", arXiv:2501.02700) announces a proof of the full conjecture using a reflection principle across the sphere; as of May 2026 this proof has been circulated but not yet recorded as fully peer-reviewed and accepted in the literature, so the status is best described as partially solved / claimed.

status_evidence.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces and the reflection principle
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a reflection principle for minimal surfaces meeting a sphere orthogonally and uses it to prove that every embedded free boundary minimal annulus in a ball is the critical catenoid.
status_evidence.claim: Claims a proof of the critical catenoid conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Sufficient symmetry conditions for free boundary minimal annuli to be the critical catenoid
status_evidence.snippet: Shows uniqueness under additional symmetry assumptions on the annulus.
status_evidence.claim: Prior partial results assumed extra symmetry.

status_evidence.title: A Characterization of the Critical Catenoid
status_evidence.snippet: Fraser–Sargent type characterization under antipodal symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier characterization of the critical catenoid under symmetry.
